title: Muffin — Data coverage
description: How complete the data is and where the gaps are. From market.coverage_sample, a twice-daily snapshot of market.coverage_current — one definition, so the table can never disagree with the view.

panels.title: Completeness RIGHT NOW, by security type
panels.description: The trend panels below need HISTORY, and coverage is sampled only TWICE A DAY behind an 11-hour gate — so after any outage they are two dots at the right-hand edge of a 30-day axis, which reads as 'No Data' even though the query returns rows. Measured 2026-08-28: exactly 2 points. This panel answers the same question from the LATEST sample alone, so the dashboard is useful on day one and while the history refills. Completeness is TYPED — market.required_facet decides what each type owes, because a bond arrives from an N-PORT filing and that is all it will ever be; one flat definition would report 55% of the universe permanently broken.

targets.rawSql:
select security_type_code as metric,
       round(100.0 * sum(complete) / nullif(sum(securities), 0), 1) as value
  from market.coverage_sample
 where sampled_at = (select max(sampled_at) from market.coverage_sample)
   and dimension = 'security_type'
 group by security_type_code
 order by 2 desc

panels.title: Completeness by security type
panels.description: Percent of each type meeting the facets ITS type requires (market.required_facet). Bonds require nothing — they arrive from an N-PORT filing and that is all they will ever be — so they sit at 100% by definition. 15,159 of 27,629 securities are bonds; a flat definition would report the majority of the universe permanently broken.

targets.rawSql:
select sampled_at as time, security_type_code as metric,
       round(100.0 * complete / nullif(securities, 0), 1) as value
  from market.coverage_sample
 where $__timeFilter(sampled_at) and dimension = 'security_type'
 order by sampled_at

panels.title: Least complete countries (latest sample)
panels.description: Where the gaps actually are. Restricted to buckets of 20+ securities: a country with three securities can be 0% complete and mean nothing.

targets.rawSql:
select bucket as "country", security_type_code as "type", securities, complete,
       round(100.0 * complete / nullif(securities,0), 1) as "complete %"
  from market.coverage_sample
 where sampled_at = (select max(sampled_at) from market.coverage_sample) and dimension = 'country' and securities >= 20
 order by 100.0 * complete / nullif(securities,0) asc nulls first
 limit 30

panels.title: Coverage matrix — which FACET is missing, by sector
panels.description: The point of storing facet counts as COLUMNS: one panel shows which facet is the bottleneck rather than a single completeness score that hides it.

targets.rawSql:
select bucket as "sector", securities,
       with_symbol as "symbol", with_sector as "sector✓", with_industry as "industry",
       with_price as "price", with_performance as "perf", with_profile as "profile",
       with_fundamentals as "fundamentals", with_statements as "statements", with_metrics as "metrics"
  from market.coverage_sample
 where sampled_at = (select max(sampled_at) from market.coverage_sample) and dimension = 'sector' and security_type_code = 'equity'
 order by securities desc

panels.title: Price freshness — securities priced in the last N days
panels.description: The gap between 'have a symbol' and 'last 30d' is the population the price pipeline is not reaching. Cheap because migration 130 indexed (date, security_id) — the same question was a Parallel Seq Scan over 10.9M rows and 11 seconds before it.

targets.rawSql:
select sampled_at as time,
       sum(priced_3d)  as "last 3d",
       sum(priced_7d)  as "last 7d",
       sum(priced_30d) as "last 30d",
       sum(with_symbol) as "have a symbol"
  from market.coverage_sample
 where $__timeFilter(sampled_at) and dimension = 'security_type'
 group by sampled_at order by sampled_at

panels.title: Completeness by MSCI tier
panels.description: Whether emerging and frontier markets are systematically under-ingested relative to developed ones. Equities only — the tier of a bond is not a meaningful lens.

targets.rawSql:
select sampled_at as time, bucket as metric,
       round(100.0 * complete / nullif(securities,0), 1) as value
  from market.coverage_sample
 where $__timeFilter(sampled_at) and dimension = 'msci_tier' and security_type_code = 'equity'
 order by sampled_at

panels.title: Completeness by market-cap band
panels.description: Coverage is usually good for mega caps and poor for small ones, because the backlogs are ordered by fund weight. This is the panel that says how bad the tail is.

targets.rawSql:
select sampled_at as time, bucket as metric,
       round(100.0 * complete / nullif(securities,0), 1) as value
  from market.coverage_sample
 where $__timeFilter(sampled_at) and dimension = 'cap_band' and security_type_code = 'equity'
 order by sampled_at

panels.title: Securities with no sector / no symbol at all
panels.description: A null dimension is a real population — 'securities with no sector' is precisely the gap this dashboard exists to show — so it is bucketed as `unknown` rather than dropped by the group by.

targets.rawSql:
select sampled_at as time,
       sum(securities) filter (where bucket = 'unknown') as "unknown bucket"
  from market.coverage_sample
 where $__timeFilter(sampled_at) and dimension = 'sector'
 group by sampled_at order by sampled_at
